governance.status: LEVEL 2 — TECHNICALLY VERIFIED, NOT EXTERNALLY ATTESTED
governance.description: Comprehensive Literature Map: peer-reviewed research, major reviews, and preprints mapped to project capabilities and structures.

literature_entries.authors: McKeon, B. J.; Sharma, A. S.
literature_entries.title: A critical-layer framework for turbulent pipe flow
literature_entries.problem_studied: Input-output formulation of wall-bounded turbulence; resolvent operator analysis of velocity response to nonlinear forcing
literature_entries.method: Singular value decomposition of the linearized Navier-Stokes resolvent operator around turbulent mean velocity profile
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Rank-1 resolvent approximation captures primary wall-attached energetic structures and logarithmic layer scaling
literature_entries.limitations: Linearized around fixed empirical mean profile; does not provide standalone closed dynamical system without nonlinear feedback closure
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Directly supports our Candidate W9-G/J ResolventResponseBasis. Resolvent modes are optimal for forcing-response and wall-layer structure modeling rather than standalone time-stepping ROM bases.

literature_entries.authors: Toedtli, S. S.; Luhar, M.; McKeon, B. J.
literature_entries.title: Predicting the response of turbulent channel flow to varying-phase opposition control: resolvent analysis as a tool for flow control design
literature_entries.problem_studied: Turbulent channel flow drag reduction and wall shear stress control under active opposition control
literature_entries.method: Resolvent-based gain analysis of input-output transfer function relating wall blowing/suction to wall shear stress modification
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Successfully predicted optimal sensor placement and phase shift for maximum wall shear stress reduction without full DNS sweeps
literature_entries.limitations: Focuses on boundary-actuated response; assumes mean profile perturbation is small or predictable
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Direct precedent for Output-Oriented / Boundary-Observable ROM. Proves that our failed W9-G resolvent basis is highly capable when redirected from full-field state reconstruction to wall-shear control design.

literature_entries.title: Interpolation method for adapting reduced-order models and application to aerostructural optimization
literature_entries.problem_studied: Reduced-order modeling across changing operating parameters and regimes where single global POD fails
literature_entries.method: Grassmann manifold interpolation of local POD basis subspaces; mapping subspaces to tangent space at reference point, interpolating, and mapping back
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Accurate prediction of aeroelastic flutter and nonlinear structural response across parameter variations without recomputing high-fidelity models
literature_entries.limitations: Requires smooth parameter-to-manifold mapping; topology of subspaces must remain compatible
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Directly explains and resolves our W3/W4 POD cross-seed failure (N02/N03). Our subspace distance metric (W4) computes the exact Grassmannian chordal distance used in this literature.

literature_entries.authors: Amsallem, D.; Zahr, M. J.; Farhat, C.
literature_entries.title: Nonlinear model order reduction based on local reduced-order bases
literature_entries.venue: International Journal for Numerical Methods in Engineering, 92(10), 891-916
literature_entries.problem_studied: Nonlinear dynamical systems with strong state-space localization or multi-regime transitions
literature_entries.method: Clustering state snapshots into localized regions, constructing local POD bases per cluster, and online nearest-neighbor/smooth switching
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Orders-of-magnitude reduction in online dimension and error compared to global POD on complex nonlinear shock and contact problems
literature_entries.limitations: Cluster boundary chattering requires smoothing/hysteresis; offline clustering cost scales with snapshot count
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Directly supports our ClusteredLocalPODBasis (R08). Proves that local clustering is the standard solution when global linear bases encounter high Kolmogorov n-width.

literature_entries.authors: Kaiser, E.; Noack, B. R.; Cordier, L.; Spohn, A.; Segond, M.; Abel, M.; Brunton, S. L.; Östh, J.; Krajnović, S.; Niven, R. K.
literature_entries.title: Cluster-based reduced-order modelling of a jet in crossflow
literature_entries.problem_studied: Strongly nonlinear, un-stationary fluid dynamics with multiple operating regimes and limit cycles
literature_entries.method: Cluster-based Reduced-Order Modeling (CROM): k-means clustering in state space combined with transition probability Markov models
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Captures multi-attractor transitions and intermittency in turbulent jet-in-crossflow without requiring globally accurate POD Galerkin ODEs
literature_entries.limitations: Probabilistic/statistical rather than deterministic trajectory prediction; resolution limited by number of cluster centroids
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Direct precedent for transitioning our failed turbulent ROM from continuous ODE integration to discrete Markovian state transitions using our existing snapshot clustering infrastructure.

literature_entries.title: Divergence-free and curl-free wavelets in two dimensions and three dimensions: application to turbulent flows
literature_entries.problem_studied: Spatial representation of incompressible velocity fields and multiscale turbulence without pressure Poisson solves
literature_entries.method: Construction of anisotropic, compactly supported, divergence-free and curl-free wavelet bases from 1D multiresolution analysis
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Exact discrete incompressibility in wavelet space; efficient nonlinear term evaluation via fast wavelet transform
literature_entries.limitations: Boundary conditions require specialized boundary wavelet constructions; non-periodic wall treatments add complexity
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Direct mathematical foundation for our W13-F / W13-G multiresolution solenoidal dictionaries. Explains why multiscale solenoidal packets are mathematically sound, while highlighting boundary wavelet challenges.

literature_entries.title: Coherent vortex extraction in three-dimensional homogeneous isotropic turbulence using orthogonal wavelets
literature_entries.problem_studied: Decomposition of turbulent velocity fields into coherent energetic vortices and incoherent Gaussian background noise
literature_entries.method: Wavelet thresholding of 3D vorticity/velocity fields; nonlinear filtering using Donoho-Johnstone universal threshold
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Retaining only ~3% of wavelet coefficients captures >99% of total kinetic energy and all non-Gaussian intermittency
literature_entries.limitations: Applied to instantaneous field denoising/compression; time-stepping the extracted sparse coherent structures requires adaptive grid tracking
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Direct validation of our SparsificationEngine participation ratio and sparsity analysis. Shows that multiscale wavelet representations excel at coherent structure extraction, even if global Galerkin time evolution is challenging.

literature_entries.title: Fourth-order time-stepping for stiff PDEs
literature_entries.problem_studied: Accurate, stable time-integration of stiff semilinear PDEs (Kuramoto-Sivashinsky, Korteweg-de Vries, reaction-diffusion, Allen-Cahn)
literature_entries.method: Exponential Time Differencing 4th-order Runge-Kutta (ETDRK4) with complex contour integration for stable evaluation of phi-functions
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Allowed timesteps 10x-100x larger than standard explicit/IMEX methods while maintaining 4th-order accuracy on stiff spatial Laplacians
literature_entries.limitations: Requires diagonal or efficiently exponential-factorizable linear operator
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Directly underpins our IntegratingFactorModalODEIntegrator (R13) and StokesEigenmodeODEIntegrator (W8). Proves our ETD implementation is universally applicable to any stiff semilinear PDE.

literature_entries.title: Exponential integrators
literature_entries.problem_studied: Comprehensive mathematical theory, stability analysis, and error bounds for exponential time differencing methods across parabolic and hyperbolic PDEs
literature_entries.method: Rigorous semigroup and sectorial operator analysis of exponential multistep and Runge-Kutta methods
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Proved unconditional stability bounds for linear parabolic parts and optimal convergence rates for semilinear parabolic systems
literature_entries.limitations: Nonlinear Lipschitz constant limits maximum explicit step; non-autonomous operators require Magnus expansions
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Provides mathematical rigor for our Hypothesis T1 (ETD for reaction-diffusion and heat equations). Formally justifies why our ETD solver achieves machine-precision linear decay.

literature_entries.authors: Reiss, J.; Schulze, P.; Sesterhenn, J.; Mehrmann, V.
literature_entries.title: The Shifted Proper Orthogonal Decomposition: A mode decomposition for multiple transport phenomena
literature_entries.venue: SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing, 40(3), A1322-A1344
literature_entries.problem_studied: Failure of classical POD on transport-dominated, wave-propagating, and advection problems (slow Kolmogorov n-width decay)
literature_entries.method: Shifted POD (sPOD): decomposing fields into superpositions of comoving reference frames with time-dependent shifts c_k(t)
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Reduces mode count by an order of magnitude for traveling waves, shocks, and convective flows compared to classical POD
literature_entries.limitations: Shift identification optimization is non-convex for multiple overlapping waves; requires shift tracking algorithms
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Directly mirrors our W4 optimal_translation_alignment and fourier_phase_amplitude_decomposition. Explains why our W3/W4 POD failed (random spatial phases) and provides the exact mathematical framework to solve it.

literature_entries.authors: Rowley, C. W.; Marsden, J. E.
literature_entries.title: Reconstruction equations and the Karhunen-Loève expansion for systems with symmetry
literature_entries.problem_studied: Model reduction of fluid flows exhibiting continuous spatial symmetries (translation, rotation)
literature_entries.method: Symmetry reduction / slice method: quotienting out the continuous group action (spatial shift) before computing POD modes
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Converts traveling wave dynamics into stationary limit cycles in the reduced quotient space, restoring fast POD eigenvalue decay
literature_entries.limitations: Requires explicit Lie group parameterization of symmetries; phase velocity must be reconstructed dynamically
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Direct mathematical foundation for our W4 phase-shift audit. Proves that factoring out spatial translations is necessary and sufficient to make POD work on translational flows.

literature_entries.title: On long-term stability of POD-Galerkin models of a plane mixing layer
literature_entries.problem_studied: Catastrophic instabilities and energy blowup in truncated quadratic POD-Galerkin fluid models
literature_entries.method: Enforcing exact skew-symmetry on modal quadratic interaction tensors and adding energy-conserving triad regularization
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Proved that strictly preserving quadratic tensor skew-symmetry is required for long-term physical boundedness without artificial dissipation
literature_entries.limitations: Skew-symmetry alone does not guarantee correct dissipation rate without subgrid closure
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Directly confirms our findings in W5/W7 (N06) that explicit triad truncation destroys energy conservation. Validates our SparseModalTensor discrete skew-symmetrization implementation.

literature_entries.title: Properties of Ramanujan filter banks
literature_entries.problem_studied: Identification of hidden integer periodicities in noisy, non-stationary time series and genomic sequences
literature_entries.method: Ramanujan periodic transforms and orthogonal Ramanujan filter banks based on arithmetic Ramanujan sums c_q(n)
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Optimal finite-duration extraction of integer-periodic components without spectral leakage inherent to short-time Fourier transforms
literature_entries.limitations: Designed for discrete integer arithmetic periodicities; not naturally adapted to continuous spatial differential operators
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Explains why RamanujanCorrection failed for continuous fluid turbulence (N01) while pointing to its legitimate application: discrete periodic signal extraction, vibration harmonic detection, and time-series decomposition.

literature_entries.authors: Majda, A. J.; Timofeyev, I.; Vanden-Eijnden, E.
literature_entries.title: Systematic strategies for stochastic mode reduction in climate
literature_entries.problem_studied: Closure modeling and dimension reduction for truncated nonlinear wave and geophysical flow systems with quadratic triad coupling
literature_entries.method: Mori-Zwanzig projection formalism and stochastic subgrid modeling derived from triad interaction structure
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Derived effective deterministic eddy damping plus stochastic backscatter terms that accurately preserve equilibrium energy spectra
literature_entries.limitations: Requires asymptotic timescale separation between resolved and unresolved modes
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Directly supports our fit_modal_eddy_viscosity (R15) and SparseTriadGraph (R10). Validates our modal closure framework from a rigorous statistical physics perspective.

literature_entries.authors: Brunton, S. L.; Noack, B. R.
literature_entries.title: Closed-loop turbulence control: Progress and challenges
literature_entries.problem_studied: State of the art in reduced-order modeling, machine learning, and sensor-based feedback control of turbulent flows
literature_entries.method: Comprehensive review of POD, DMD, resolvent analysis, clustered ROM, and output-oriented control strategies
literature_entries.demonstrated_result: Showed that successful control does NOT require full-field state reconstruction; low-rank models targeting specific boundary observables (wall shear, lift, drag) are far more effective
literature_entries.limitations: Review paper; highlights that full-state universal turbulence ROM remains open, while observable-specific control is mature
literature_entries.relationship_to_our_capability: Authoritative validation of our P1/P2 core thesis: our project failed at the overly ambitious target (universal full-state turbulent compression), but succeeded at the building blocks for observable-specific and boundary-oriented modeling.
